our_side: One seat (ai 0, team 1), Armada (lobby side random, played arm) from H7 (3764, 3287) in the south-east box. Player: Claude Opus 5.5 at effort low (claude2 account), realtime, via run/human_game.sh. result.minute: about 12:34 (the commander at 100% at 12:22 and 5% at 12:33, at G6 beside the lab; the record ends there; a lobby game with no results row)

summary: One Opus 5.5 low seat (Armada, south-east) played the user himself (computer_whisperer, Armada, north-west) in realtime on Avalanche 3.4 and lost at about 12:34 when its commander died at home. The pre-game role-word list was in force at 0:02, but the player's 0:10 turn swapped its solars and third extractor for seven wind turbines, and at 1:50, in a wind lull with the energy store empty, listed two more turbines ahead of the first constructor's extractors: ten turbines by 2:20, the energy store full and metal at 0 from 3:00, two extractors from 0:15 to 3:08 and never more than six of our ten spots (income 3.5-11.6). His Pawns were in our half from 2:18; at 4:01-4:10 two parties split our one Pawn group, which switched target four times, and four extractors fell by 5:31 with no raiding party paying. Our one counter-raid (12 Pawns, 6:25) killed his E4 outpost and was walked home by a since-fixed losses-line defect; his factory was never seen. From 8:27 his Maces and Centurions (reach 380 against the Pawns' 180) beat our Pawns at F4/F5, walked into the base at 10:55 while our army was at D6 against his turret creep (1,272 lost for 530), and killed the commander at the lab at 12:23-12:33.

root.what: The player's second turn replaced the pre-game list already in force (two extractors, three solars, lab, assist, a third extractor) with seven wind turbines and no third extractor; the commander built turbines and the lab, and the seat held two extractors until 3:08 on 5.5 metal a second.

our_mistakes.what: Rewrote a correct pre-game list: the third extractor dropped and seven turbines put on the commander. A stronger player keeps the extractors first (spot_13, spot_18 at 684, spot_11 at 924) and adds generators only as the lab's draw requires.
our_mistakes.evidence: 0:10 queue (the root); the player's text: 'I swapped the solar generators for wind turbines, which follows the experienced players' advice on a windy map'; analyze_match extractors 2 at minutes 1, 2, 3

our_mistakes.what: Stationed the Pawns at spot_11 (G5) and told them to send one or two against a lone raider: Pawn hunts of equal speed caught nothing, the H7/H8 home spots were 600-900 from the group, and no Sentry stood at a home spot when they fell. A stronger player keeps the body on the spots it defends and puts a Sentry beside each.
our_mistakes.evidence: 0:10 instruct: 'then they hold at spot_11, attacking enemy raiders ... (send one or two against a lone raider)'; raid_ledger: 'answered 10 (median delay 1.0 s); parties that paid 0'; first armllt created 3:01

our_mistakes.what: Read a wind lull as an energy shortage and put two more turbines ahead of the constructor's extractors, under the solar rule the player had copied into its instructions; by 2:50 the store was full and metal at 0. A stronger player lets the store run low behind the plant (the bound was metal) or builds a solar, which needs no energy to build.
our_mistakes.evidence: 1:50 report: 'energy 0/1152 ... STALLING ... wind now 8'; queue constructor_15805 [armwin, armwin, extractor spot_18, ...]; 3:00 report: 'metal 0 (+5.5/-4.9), energy 1204/1204 (+150), wind now 15'

our_mistakes.what: No scouting: his factory was never seen and nothing of ours came within 1,500 of his start, so his switch to Maces was met only when it arrived at 8:27. A stronger player keeps a Pawn or a radar on his side and switches the lab when the first Mace shows.
our_mistakes.evidence: minutes.py: 'his first factory seen: never'; 'first of ours within 1,500 of his start (B1): never'; 8:42 produce lab_6376 [armham]

our_mistakes.what: One group answered two parties by switching between them every few seconds (the hands' picks, on the player's single-group station); two halves, or the group on one pair and the commander on the other, would have saved one pair.
our_mistakes.evidence: hands_window 4:01 attack party_3, 4:04 party_4, 4:08 party_3, 4:10 party_4; raid_ledger 4:02 spot_18 and 4:10 spot_15, 10 soldiers within 900 each

our_mistakes.what: Sent the whole army to D6 to clear a turret creep while his main army was unseen in our half; it was about 1,400 from the base when party_7 came. A stronger player answers a creep with a few units or the turrets' reach and keeps the body home while the Mace army is about.
our_mistakes.evidence: 10:11 instruct: 'group_K1 attacks his buildings and constructor at spot_12 now, all together, then walks back and holds at spot_11'; party_7 last fought at F5 9:35-9:54 (#5); review.md: K1's front at D6, tail at E7 at 10:55

their_play: computer_whisperer (the user, Armada, B1) opened with Pawns across the map: one in our half at 2:18, raids at G7 from 2:48, two parties at once (3 at H7/H8, 4 at H5) at 4:00-4:10 and parties of three at 5:03 and 5:31, taking four extractors while no raiding party of his was paid for. He held an outpost at E4 (extractor, Sentry, constructor; seen 6:25) and later crept Sentries onto our spot_12 at D6 (9:54-10:24). By 8:27 he had switched to Maces and Centurions (reach 380 and 325 against the Pawns' 180): the army came in at F4/F5 (8:30-9:54), left sight, came back into G5/G6 at 10:55 while our army was at D6, withdrew at 11:29 and returned to finish the base and the commander at 12:18-12:33. His factory, economy and tier were never seen (no truth file: what we saw are floors; party_7 read 790 to 1,870 metal).

bears_on.note: Lost on extractors before the fights: two extractors to 3:08, never more than six of our ten spots, income 3.5-11.6; every later fight was fought on that (the reader's reading; nobody said it in this game).
We never held half the map: at most 6 of 19 spots (11:00), all in our half; his extractor count is unknown (no truth file).

The 0:10 swap cited 'the experienced players' advice on a windy map' (this lesson's 'go wind for the rest of their e'), but dropped the rest of the same lines: '2 mex, wind ... one construction bot expanding' and 'solar is better when you are out of e, because you do not e stall making solar' (turbines queued into an empty store at 1:50).
The wind-map form of the same over-build: ten turbines by 2:20, the energy store full at 2:50-3:00 with metal at 0; the lesson itself is about solars on Comet.
From his side: his first Pawn was in our half at 2:18 and his Pawn parties took four extractors 4:02-5:31; ours first crossed at 6:35 and never came within 1,500 of his start.
Our one raid stopped at his E4 outpost and was walked home at 6:37 (a since-fixed losses-line defect) instead of going on to spot_6/3/4 as the player's 6:04 note planned.
Detachments of 2-4 against single Pawns (2:48-3:05, 8:27-8:39) and the army strung from D6 to E7, about 1,400 from the base, when his army came at 10:55.
The bot form of the light-to-medium switch, played against us: his Maces and Centurions beat our Pawns at F4 (405 for 0) and F5 (436 for 54); our lab switched at 8:42, after they arrived.

tools: record-0.jsonl and strategist-0.jsonl read directly (turbine and extractor events, the commander's health samples, the turns' texts)
lens.caveats: No truth file, results row or batch file (a lobby game): his numbers are what we saw, floors. pro_baseline.py not run (not Comet; the review found no Avalanche cards); floor.py's result and minutes columns blank. The user was the opponent and typed no chat, so the only person's word on this game is his post-game ruling in docs/knowledge/jev.md (2026-10-03, after reviewing player-44 and human-11): 'The thrash hasn't been a huge problem in this game and in player-44 ... I would call that fix a success'. The thrash counts and the 9:32 lateness are the existing review's, not recounted. Built on review.md and agrees with its root (0:10). Differs on: the raid war's root (the player's 0:10 station at spot_11 and 'send one or two' clause, before the 2:48 churn the review names); the 1:50 stall being a wind lull answered under the player's copied solar rule; the 10:11 order answering his turret creep on our spot_12 (the review frames it as an attack on an outpost); and the commander's end (the review has the 12:23 attack under 'everything attacks party_7 now', but that turn began at 12:25; the 12:23 attack was under the 12:15 orders, and the 12:25 instruction had landed by the 12:30 pick, which attacked at 24% health against its own health clause). The review places the end at H6; analyze_match and the record put the commander at G6 beside the lab.

open_questions: His economy and timings are unknown (no truth file): when did his Maces start, and how many extractors did he hold at 4:00 and 8:00? The replay or the user could answer.
Was the D6 Sentry creep (9:54-10:24) meant to draw our army out before the 10:55 attack? (the reader's reading; the user played it)

At 1:18 the places audit marked the first constructor's gate a fault (asked about spot_12 alone while spot_18/11/8 stood open at 0.58-0.64): the places layer or the openers layer? (the review's candidate)

Why did the 12:30 world pick undo the commander's walk at 24% health with 'Under a third health it walks to spot_18' in the instructions: does the player's 'everything attacks party_7 now' outrank its own health clause for Jev?
Would wind as the generator have been right on Avalanche's 3-19 wind had the extractor steps been kept? The finding is the count and the dropped extractor, not the choice.
